is_anopheles.evidence: Studies Anopheles gambiae s.l. (specifically An. gambiae s.s.) and Anopheles funestus s.l. (page 4).

reports_target_markers.evidence: Tested for both Leu-Phe (west, Vgsc L995F) and Leu-Ser (east, Vgsc L995S) kdr mutations (page 4 and page 6).

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: Table 5 provides exact counts of homozygous Leu-Phe mutation, heterozygous Leu-Phe mutation, and homozygous wild type for 159 An. gambiae s.s. across 5 sites (Chipepo, Myooye, Chipulukusu, Kizhingezhinge, Mushili), and reports all 159 were negative for east kdr.

african_field_population.evidence: Mosquitoes were collected during the rainy seasons of 2009 and 2010 from localities in Zambia as larvae or indoor resting blood-fed females and reared to adults (page 3-4).

is_primary_study.evidence: Primary research article reporting field collections, WHO bioassays, and molecular genotyping in Zambia.

sub_country_location.evidence: Named localities/sentinel sites in Zambia including Chipepo, Myooye, Chipulukusu, Kizhingezhinge, and Mushili (Table 5).

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: Mosquitoes for resistance testing were collected during the rainy seasons of 2009 and 2010 (page 3-4).

duplicate_risk.evidence: Primary field survey conducted in Zambia under national monitoring/evaluation supported by IVCC.

supplement.evidence: All genotype data (Table 5) and bioassay data (Tables 3-4) are reported in the main text.

assessment.summary: This study evaluated vector abundance, sporozoite infection rates, WHO susceptibility assays, and kdr mutations in Anopheles gambiae s.s. and Anopheles funestus in Zambia during 2009-2010. Genotyping of 159 bioassay survivors across 5 localities revealed the presence of the Vgsc L995F (Leu-Phe) mutation and absence of Vgsc L995S (Leu-Ser), with complete genotype counts presented in Table 5.
